headline: Buckshot Bourbon joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Buckshot Bourbon — Country Rock from Anywhere, NY.
body:
Buckshot Bourbon have joined Quantum Frequency Records. A country-rock outfit that treats the open road like a studio. Buckshot Bourbon writes bar-room hymns with arena-sized choruses — whiskey-warm guitars, stacked harmonies, and stories that refuse to sand off their edges.

Buckshot Bourbon started as a Friday-night residency in a converted feed mill north of the city. What began as three-hour sets for regulars became a catalog of songs about work, weather, loyalty, and the kind of love that leaves boot prints. headline: Sawyer Kennedy joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Sawyer Kennedy — Nashville Country from Nashville, TN.
body:
Sawyer Kennedy have joined Quantum Frequency Records. A solo Nashville country artist who writes like a novelist and sings like the last person left in the room. Sawyer Kennedy's catalog is intimate, cinematic, and unafraid of silence.

Sawyer Kennedy moved to Nashville with a notebook and a borrowed Telecaster. After two winters of writer's rounds and one very public breakup record, the songs started traveling further than the gigs. QFR heard a demo of 'Glass Off the Dashboard' and offered a home that would not force a radio template onto a storyteller. headline: Fractal Hearts joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Fractal Hearts — Progressive / Space Rock from Portland, OR.
body:
Fractal Hearts have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Progressive, cosmic, and meticulously built. Fractal Hearts treat albums like constellations — motifs return, time signatures tilt, and guitars bloom into atmospheres.

Fractal Hearts formed in a Portland rehearsal loft after a failed jazz-fusion project and a successful all-night planetarium shift. Their music folds math-rock discipline into space-rock wonder. QFR signed them for the ambition: records that reward headphones, stages that reward patience, and a visual language of recursive geometry. Live, they run a three-screen light plot designed by the drummer.

headline: Grassroots Rebellion joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Grassroots Rebellion — Punk Rock from Brooklyn, NY.
body:
Grassroots Rebellion have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Punk rock with pop-punk adrenaline and alt-rock craft. Grassroots Rebellion write two-minute arguments you can shout from a sticky floor.

Grassroots Rebellion came up on basement bills, community radio, and a photocopied zine that outlived three practice spaces. Their songs are short, sharp, and surprisingly tender in the third verse. QFR wanted a band that could sit next to country and nu-metal without blinking — GR is that band. They still run their own merch table.

The Warpnotix project is a laboratory for dance-floor physics: sub that you feel in your ribs, breaks that reset the room, and a visual identity of warped grids. headline: Sound Shamans joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Sound Shamans — Alt / Indie Rock from Austin, TX.
body:
Sound Shamans have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Alt-rock built on hypnotic riffs, desert air, and a live reputation that borders on ceremony. Sound Shamans treat volume as a language.

Sound Shamans emerged from Austin's late-night circuit with a reputation for sets that felt longer than the clock. They write in cycles and drones, then smash those cycles with choruses. The band's visual world is ochre, bone, and blue-black night. QFR brought them in to hold the indie/alt lane without turning it into a costume.

headline: Immovable Giants joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Immovable Giants — Alt / Indie Rock from Chicago, IL.
body:
Immovable Giants have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Chicago alt-rock that builds cathedrals out of patience. Immovable Giants write slow-burn anthems for people who stayed.

Immovable Giants have been a Chicago secret for a decade: winter records, sold-out rooms, and a refusal to hurry. Their songs start small and become inevitable. QFR signed them to give the catalog a backbone of adult, unshowy rock — the kind that still hits like weather. The band records to tape when the song asks for it and to a laptop when it doesn't.

headline: The Jones Beach Boys joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes The Jones Beach Boys — Surf Rock from Long Island, NY.
body:
The Jones Beach Boys have joined Quantum Frequency Records. A 1960s-surf-influenced group that treats the shoreline as a time machine. Twang, harmony, and summer even in January.

The Jones Beach Boys started as a joke name and became a real band the night they learned four-part surf harmony in a parking lot. They write instrumentals and vocal tunes with equal love for spring reverb and unsarcastic joy. QFR signed them because the roster needed sun — and because the songs are better than nostalgia. They record live in a beach bungalow when the weather allows.

headline: The Cosmic Run joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes The Cosmic Run — Alt / Folk Rock from Boulder, CO.
body:
The Cosmic Run have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Alt-folk-rock that starts on a trail and ends in orbit. Acoustic bones, electric weather, and lyrics that look both inward and up.

The Cosmic Run write on long drives and longer hikes. Their records move from fingerpicked confessionals to wide, night-sky rock without losing the plot. QFR heard them as the connective tissue of the roster — the band that makes country fans stay for the psych set. They self-produce with a mobile rig and a stubborn love of first takes.

headline: Moonflower Radio joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Moonflower Radio — Psychedelic Rock from San Francisco, CA.
body:
Moonflower Radio have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Psychedelic alt-rock transmitted like a late-night station from another decade. Pedals, poetry, and patiently exploding choruses.

Moonflower Radio have always sounded like a broadcast you found by accident and then never left. They came out of San Francisco's psych revival without becoming a museum act. QFR signed them for the color they add to the universe — washed-out film, analog delay, and lyrics that treat consciousness as a collaborative instrument. Their live shows are famously long and famously kind.

headline: Find/Replace joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Find/Replace — Industrial / Nu-Metal from Detroit, MI.
body:
Find/Replace have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Industrial rock colliding with nu-metal weight. Find/Replace write about systems, glitches, and the people caught in the search field.

Find/Replace formed in a Detroit warehouse that used to stamp auto parts. The building's acoustics — and its ghosts — are in the records. They sample factory ambience, scream like a UI error, and still write choruses you can put a fist in the air for. QFR wanted industrial muscle without corporate dystopia-as-cosplay. Find/Replace is the real weather of a city that makes things.

headline: Immortal Prophets joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Immortal Prophets — Nu-Metal from Cleveland, OH.
body:
Immortal Prophets have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Nu-metal with a philosophical streak. Immortal Prophets write about fate, fury, and the joke of being mortal at this volume.

Immortal Prophets came out of Cleveland's heavy circuit with riffs that felt both vintage-2000 and unnervingly current. They rap, they scream, they stack gang vocals, and they mean it. QFR signed them to hold the heavy lane with dignity — no nostalgia trap, no irony shield. The band's mythos is self-made: sigils, sermons, and a live show that feels like a rite.

headline: Firewall Nation joins the Quantum Frequency roster
excerpt: Quantum Frequency Records welcomes Firewall Nation — Nu-Metal / Rap Rock from Atlanta, GA.
body:
Firewall Nation have joined Quantum Frequency Records. Nu-metal colliding with rap-rock cadence. Firewall Nation write about networks, loyalty, and what gets through.

Firewall Nation started as a cypher that needed guitars. Atlanta's rap precision met Midwestern heaviness after a tour van accident (minor, mythologized) put a producer and a metal guitarist in the same waiting room. The result is a band that can cut a verse like a verse and a chorus like a wall. QFR signed them as proof that the roster's 'nation' is bigger than any one scene.
